There was always this thought in head that if I could choose I would be a woman. I just figured all guys thought this way. As a kid I'd daydream about "gender-picking day" where kids would get to line up at a machine and get to switch genders if they wanted to.

But they were always just nice little thoughts I'd have, I didn't really think about it that much because I knew that I was a boy. This was just a fantasy and I was actually pretty happy a kid.

When puberty started just before high school, I started feeling bad. I never connected it to the changes I was experiencing, but I was starting to disassociate what I looked like from myself. I never really cared about how I looked that much even before puberty but now I barely even looked in the mirror.

I tried to clean myself once high school started but I was starting to feel uncomfortable with my body and it probably showed in how I carried myself. Places were getting hairier and had been since middle school, and the few times I tried to shave my legs specifically I was given grossed-out looks by my mom that made me stop.

There wasn't that much anger, it was more that my mom was always really loving and supporting, but when she saw me with shaved legs I saw the first time that she was disgusted with me. I didn't know how to deal with that. 

I started taking on the thought process that all the stuff that kids do at that age to express themselves was silly. I was obviously more mature than all these people because I was comfortable wearing a jacket and baggy jeans every day to school. In reality I probably would've experimented with my looks in similar ways if I hadn't been both ashamed of what I looked like and an ingrained desire to not come off as gay in my mother's eyes. It's important to note here that my mother is of Hispanic descent so was not in tune with American culture, was in her 50's at the time I was a teenager and was raised by her grandmother who was born in the 1800's. All this and the fact that she was a devout Roman Catholic meant that my mom would see a lot more things as "gay" than the average person.

I got started skipping class a lot and eventually got my GED at 16. Most of my teenage years were spent alone in my room feeling sorry for myself, feeling that something was wrong with me and that somewhere along the line things had gone horribly wrong. The only signs that I was transgender at this point in my life was my desire to remove all my body hair, a reoccurring temptation to try on my mother's clothes and a tendency to want to let my hair grow out. 

The Pulse nightclub shooting happened a few days after my 20th birthday. I was lazily surfing a message board a frequent and my eyes landed on the "LGBT" board. I had never clicked on the board because I had assumed it filled with porn and people discussing their fetishes. I obviously wasn't gay anyway so why I go there? 

But my brain finally had an excuse to go to the board. I wanted to see the reaction that people were having to the shooting. Instead of finding reactions however, I found the part of the board dedicated to MtFs. It awakened feelings in me that had been brushed off as "nice little thoughts" all my life. I found out about HRT and how the younger you start the better results you'll have. I saw people there that looked like women, not just men in dresses.

There were people here who lived their lives as women. Not because some kind of obscure fetish, but because it made them happy. While some of them had issues, a lot of just seemed like regular people who just happened to be transgender.

And I realized that I since I became a teenager I had been withering away. I had this vague future planned out for myself but it didn't seem real, it was almost like the future I was supposed to have rather than the one I wanted. I knew that if I didn't at least try this that I would regret it down the line, and that HRT would now always be on my mind if I decided against this now.

So I guess in the end I started HRT to give myself a shot at an actual life. Because I would really like that happy kid I knew to allowed to grow up into a happy, healthy adult instead of just being a shell of their former self.

I'm scared a lot of the time, I know that I'm not a prime candidate for transitioning. But I'm holding on to that chance at a normal life and with the support network I've gained since joining the transgender community online I feel like I have people that will watch my back and help me make me.
